calls.head: Top line on top line: Wilson vs. Kaprizov
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Dubois and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kaprizov reaches 500 points as the Wild beat the Capitals
paras: David Špaček picked up his first NHL point. Quinn Hughes and Michael McCarron scored less than two minutes apart early in the first to put the Wild up 2-0. Justin Sourdif got the Capitals on the board with just six seconds left in the second, but they got no closer. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-1 for the Wild on the power play with less than three minutes left, and that was that. Kirill Kaprizov added an empty-net goal with just under a minute left to make it 4-1, his 500th NHL point. Danila Yurov made it 5-1 with 25 seconds left.
The chances were closer than the score. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves for the Wild, and Logan Thompson stopped 24 of 28 at the other end.
Tom Wilson picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Wild improved to 10-3-3, still first in the Central, while the Capitals fell to 8-5-0, third in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Joel Eriksson Ek passed Andrew Brunette for tenth on the Wild’s all-time assists list, with 204.
The Capitals’ three-game winning streak is over.
The Wild have points in five straight games (4-0-1).
